entities.summary: Emerik Derenčin was a Hungarian-Croatian nobleman remembered as the commander of the Croatian troops in the 1493 Battle of Krbava Field. He was born in 1500 in a prominent noble family and received a comprehensive education in Latin, Greek, and military tactics. Derenčin's strategic leadership and bravery during the battle against the Ottoman Empire significantly contributed to the Croatian defense, which held off the invasion for several years. The Battle of Krbava Field marked a turning point in the history of Croatia, as it allowed the country to maintain its independence and sovereignty in the face of Turkish expansion. In the aftermath of the battle, Derenčin was hailed as a national hero and his name became synonymous with bravery and military prowess. Despite his significance in Croatian history, Derenčin's life and legacy have been largely overlooked by modern historians, who have instead focused on more prominent figures from the time period.
